sourceBoundary.statement: The full 179-check core gate applies to the renderer/configuration foundation. The later terminal/publication guard has the focused checks below; no post-guard full-core run is claimed.

scope: Original renderer/session/context ownership for remote Frame evaluation, supported handles and lazy FrameLocator element evaluation. Captured callbacks never replay in successor documents.
URL, blob and nested application workers and audio worklets resume and execute; this does not implement public Worker APIs.
Both registration orders reject unsupported remote scripts/routes and preserve bounded cleanup. Remote attachment permanently makes that context storage collection unsupported.
Root detachment rejects unpublished allocation, closes a published page once and settles pending operations while preserving the original failure. Child detachment keeps its parent usable.
Six unchanged upstream SVGOMG tests pass through fresh packed consumers with package-import changes only. The live demo assets are identified before/after; this is not an offline corpus.

terminalGuard.nativeTargetCleanup: Both root cases retain Target.closeTarget and original Target.targetDestroyed before context disposal.
terminalGuard.lifecycleRunBoundary: The aggregate watchdog expired after 18 completed, individually successful modules; the remaining five modules passed under separate watchdogs. All 23 individual module watchdogs exited cleanly without survivors.

retainedDevelopmentFailures: Initial SVGOMG attempt passed three candidate tests and failed three while application workers remained paused; all six passed after worker resume and remote evaluation fixes.

Initial routing restoration probe closed the whole context because the cleanup cancellation sender was dropped. Retaining the sender makes the identical controlled enable-failure probe preserve the remaining page.

Stock headless shell kept the cross-site fixture in one renderer on both engines. Its failed remote-boundary assertion is a fixture-placement mismatch, not remote-frame conformance. Full Chrome produced actual remote sessions on both engines.

Root-detachment attempts001 used an invalid protocol command ID and unrecognized encoded sentinels; child attempt002 addressed detach through the wrong parent. These are harness errors, retained separately from native engine regressions.
Terminal host compile and assertion corrections are retained privately; runtime code was unchanged by those test corrections.

reproduction.environment: Set FLASHWRIGHT_BROWSER_PATH to the pinned full Chrome binary and FLASHWRIGHT_DRIVER_PATH to a remapped build for the selected source commit. Use the external tools/watchdog.py supervisor.
reproduction.artifactPolicy: This is a portable development summary with original report hashes and selected complete outcome tables, not a raw-evidence export. Raw protocol, watchdog, reporter and fault-harness records remain private development evidence.

limitations: No performance, native Linux, release or exhaustive Playwright parity claim.
Remote locator input, general locator reads/assertions, remote network delivery/body custody, console/pageerror delivery and remote DOM/ARIA artifacts remain outside this slice.
Remote routing/init scripts, storage collection and networkidle are rejected explicitly within the stated admission boundaries.
Stock headless-shell remote placement is unverified; no altered browser placement flags were used.
The reviewed entry count remains unchanged; broader API options require their own evidence.
